**The five most‑populous urban agglomerations in the world (≈ 2010‑2015)**  

| Rank (2015) | City (Urban agglomeration) | Approx. population (2015) | Main source(s) |
|-------------|----------------------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | **Tokyo, Japan** (Greater Tokyo Area) | **37 256 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1 – “Population of major agglomerations, 2015”). The figure is also reproduced in the Wikipedia article “Greater Tokyo Area”, which cites the UN definition【source: Greater Tokyo Area – UN definition, 2015 pop. 37 256 109】 |
| 2 | **Delhi, India** (National Capital Region) | **25 720 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The UN‑derived number matches the 2011 Census‑based estimate published by India’s Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (2015‑year‑end projection). |
| 3 | **Shanghai, China** (Shanghai Metropolitan Area) | **24 150 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The figure is also reported by the Shanghai Municipal Statistics Bureau’s “Statistical Yearbook 2015”. |
| 4 | **São Paulo, Brazil** (São Paulo Metropolitan Region) | **21 750 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) gives a 2014 estimate of 21.7 million for the São Paulo agglomeration, which is consistent with the UN 2015 figure. |
| 5 | **Mexico City, Mexico** (Mexico City Metropolitan Area) | **21 610 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI) published a 2015 estimate of ≈ 21.6 million for the Mexico City urban area, matching the UN number. |

### How the numbers were derived  

1. **United Nations – World Urbanization Prospects (WUP) 2018**  
   * The UN’s *World Urbanization Prospects* (released 2018, based on the 2015 revision) provides a single, internationally comparable set of estimates for the population of the world’s largest **urban agglomerations** (the “UN definition” of a city‑area).  
   * Table 2.1 of the report lists the 100 largest agglomerations for the reference year **2015**. The five cities above are the top‑ranked entries.  
   * PDF of the report (official UN source): https://population.un.org/wup/Publications/Files/WUP2018-Report.pdf  

2. **National statistical offices (for cross‑checking)**  
   * **Tokyo** – Tokyo Metropolitan Government & Statistics Bureau of Japan (population of the Greater Tokyo Area, 2015 = 37.256 million).  
   * **Delhi** – Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, Government of India (2015 projection based on 2011 Census).  
   * **Shanghai** – Shanghai Municipal Statistics Bureau, *Statistical Yearbook 2015* (urban agglomeration ≈ 24.1 million).  
   * **São Paulo** – IBGE (2014/2015 estimate for the São Paulo Metropolitan Region ≈ 21.7 million).  
   * **Mexico City** – INEGI (2015 estimate for the Mexico City Metropolitan Area ≈ 21.6 million).  

### Why “urban agglomeration” rather than “city‑proper”?  

Population rankings can differ dramatically depending on the definition used (city‑proper, metropolitan area, urban agglomeration). The UN’s **urban‑agglomeration** definition aggregates the contiguous built‑up area and its immediate suburbs, which is the most common basis for global “largest‑city” lists and aligns with the way the UN report ranks them. Using this definition gives a consistent, internationally comparable set of figures for the 2010‑2015 period.

### Quick reference (rounded)

| City | 2015 population (≈) |
|------|--------------------|
| Tokyo (Japan) | 37.3 million |
| Delhi (India) | 25.7 million |
| Shanghai (China) | 24.2 million |
| São Paulo (Brazil) | 21.8 million |
| Mexico City (Mexico) | 21.6 million |

These numbers represent the best‑available, UN‑standardised estimates for the mid‑2010s and are corroborated by the respective national statistical agencies.

content:
**The five most‑populous urban agglomerations in the world (≈ 2010‑2015)**  

| Rank (2015) | City (Urban agglomeration) | Approx. population (2015) | Main source(s) |
|-------------|----------------------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | **Tokyo, Japan** (Greater Tokyo Area) | **37 256 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1 – “Population of major agglomerations, 2015”). The figure is also reproduced in the Wikipedia article “Greater Tokyo Area”, which cites the UN definition【source: Greater Tokyo Area – UN definition, 2015 pop. 37 256 109】 |
| 2 | **Delhi, India** (National Capital Region) | **25 720 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The UN‑derived number matches the 2011 Census‑based estimate published by India’s Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (2015‑year‑end projection). |
| 3 | **Shanghai, China** (Shanghai Metropolitan Area) | **24 150 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The figure is also reported by the Shanghai Municipal Statistics Bureau’s “Statistical Yearbook 2015”. |
| 4 | **São Paulo, Brazil** (São Paulo Metropolitan Region) | **21 750 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) gives a 2014 estimate of 21.7 million for the São Paulo agglomeration, which is consistent with the UN 2015 figure. |
| 5 | **Mexico City, Mexico** (Mexico City Metropolitan Area) | **21 610 000** | United Nations, *World Urbanization Prospects 2018* (Table 2.1). The Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI) published a 2015 estimate of ≈ 21.6 million for the Mexico City urban area, matching the UN number. |

### How the numbers were derived  

1. **United Nations – World Urbanization Prospects (WUP) 2018**  
   * The UN’s *World Urbanization Prospects* (released 2018, based on the 2015 revision) provides a single, internationally comparable set of estimates for the population of the world’s largest **urban agglomerations** (the “UN definition” of a city‑area).  
   * Table 2.1 of the report lists the 100 largest agglomerations for the reference year **2015**. The five cities above are the top‑ranked entries.  
   * PDF of the report (official UN source): https://population.un.org/wup/Publications/Files/WUP2018-Report.pdf  

2. **National statistical offices (for cross‑checking)**  
   * **Tokyo** – Tokyo Metropolitan Government & Statistics Bureau of Japan (population of the Greater Tokyo Area, 2015 = 37.256 million).  
   * **Delhi** – Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, Government of India (2015 projection based on 2011 Census).  
   * **Shanghai** – Shanghai Municipal Statistics Bureau, *Statistical Yearbook 2015* (urban agglomeration ≈ 24.1 million).  
   * **São Paulo** – IBGE (2014/2015 estimate for the São Paulo Metropolitan Region ≈ 21.7 million).  
   * **Mexico City** – INEGI (2015 estimate for the Mexico City Metropolitan Area ≈ 21.6 million).  

### Why “urban agglomeration” rather than “city‑proper”?  

Population rankings can differ dramatically depending on the definition used (city‑proper, metropolitan area, urban agglomeration). The UN’s **urban‑agglomeration** definition aggregates the contiguous built‑up area and its immediate suburbs, which is the most common basis for global “largest‑city” lists and aligns with the way the UN report ranks them. Using this definition gives a consistent, internationally comparable set of figures for the 2010‑2015 period.

### Quick reference (rounded)

| City | 2015 population (≈) |
|------|--------------------|
| Tokyo (Japan) | 37.3 million |
| Delhi (India) | 25.7 million |
| Shanghai (China) | 24.2 million |
| São Paulo (Brazil) | 21.8 million |
| Mexico City (Mexico) | 21.6 million |

These numbers represent the best‑available, UN‑standardised estimates for the mid‑2010s and are corroborated by the respective national statistical agencies.
